title: The Community Garden
story: Omar met Greta at the community garden on Sunday morning. She gave him a pair of gloves and showed him a small plot by the gate. Weeds covered the soil, and the path beside the plot was narrow. Greta showed him which leaves were weeds and which were young plants. Omar pulled the weeds slowly so he would not break the good roots. Then Greta filled a can at the tap. She said the seedlings needed gentle watering, not a flood. Omar poured a little water around each small stem. The soil turned dark and soft. Greta handed him a packet of lettuce seeds and pointed to an empty row. He made a shallow line with a stick and placed the seeds along it. He covered them with a thin layer of soil. An older member waved from the next plot and lent him a spare trowel. At noon they sat on a bench and shared two apples. Greta said the harvest would come in a few weeks if the soil stayed damp. Omar wrote the watering days on a card and pinned it inside the shed. Before he left, he washed the tools and hung the gloves on a nail. His back was tired, but the plot looked open and neat. He planned to return on Wednesday to look for the first shoots. The garden felt larger once he had work of his own inside it.
